### Installation and Environment Setup

#### Immcantation

* First, [immcantation v.4.4.0](https://hub.docker.com/r/immcantation/suite) was downloaded via Docker

```
docker pull immcantation/suite:4.4.0
```

## IgBLAST Installation

We are downloading: `ncbi-igblast-1.17.1-x64-macosx.tar.gz` from [Index of /blast/executables/igblast/release/LATEST](https://ftp.ncbi.nih.gov/blast/executables/igblast/release/LATEST/). Note that we are not downloading the `.dmg`.

For setup information, we rely on NCBI's official [How to Setup](https://ncbi.github.io/igblast/cook/How-to-set-up.html), as well as: [Using IgBlast with Python](https://github.com/xinyu-dev/igblast/blob/master/Using%20IgBlast.ipynb).

#### Required Files:

**From Troy Hinckley:**

```
alpaca_gl.aux
alpaca_new.ndm.imgt
imgt_alpaca_ig_d.fasta
imgt_alpaca_ig_j.fasta
imgt_alpaca_ig_v.fasta
```

We unzip the tar file, and we create a `database` directory in the `igblast` folder, so its contents look something like:

```
----igblast
  --bin
  --internal_data
  --optional_file
  --ChangeLog
  --LICENSE
  --ncbi_pakacage_info
  --README
  --database
```

We then create `alpaca`, and `alpaca_clean` within the `database` directory

```
----igblast
  --bin
  --internal_data
  --optional_file
  --ChangeLog
  --LICENSE
  --ncbi_pakacage_info
  --README
  ----database
    --alpaca
    --alpaca_clean
```

### Processing IMGT V(D)J sequences received from Troy

To parse the IGHV/D/J protein germline sequences, navigate to `ncbi-igblast-1.17.1`, then run:


```{bash, echo = T, eval = F}
# Process V segment sequences with edit_imgt_file
bin/edit_imgt_file.pl database/alpaca/IG_DNA/imgt_gapped_alpaca_IGHV > database/alpaca_vhh_clean/alpaca_V
# Process D segment sequences with edit_imgt_file
bin/edit_imgt_file.pl database/alpaca/IG_DNA/imgt_gapped_alpaca_IGHD > database/alpaca_vhh_clean/alpaca_D
# Process J segment sequences with edit_imgt_file
bin/edit_imgt_file.pl database/alpaca/IG_DNA/imgt_gapped_alpaca_IGHJ > database/alpaca_vhh_clean/alpaca_J
```

Note that we do not use file extensions on `alpaca_V`, `alpaca_D`, and `alpaca_J`


### Make Database

Now we make the blastdb

```{bash, echo = T, eval = F}
bin/makeblastdb -parse_seqids -dbtype nucl -in database/alpaca_vhh_clean/alpaca_V
bin/makeblastdb -parse_seqids -dbtype nucl -in database/alpaca_vhh_clean/alpaca_D
bin/makeblastdb -parse_seqids -dbtype nucl -in database/alpaca_vhh_clean/alpaca_J
```

### Moving Data to Internal Data Directory

Now we make the `alpaca` directory with `mkdir ~/ncbi-igblast-1.17.1/interal_data/alpaca`, and copy our database over from `database/alpaca_vhh_clean`.

```{bash, echo = T, eval = F}
cp -R ./database/alpaca_vhh_clean ./internal_data
```

### alpaca.ndm.imgt

Ensure that `alpaca.ndm.imgt` (which we received from TH, and is called `alpaca_new.ndm.imgt`, so need's to be renamed) is also placed in the `internal_data/alpaca` directory.

### alpaca_gl.aux

Ensure that `alpaca_gl.aux` (which we received from TH), is placed in the `optional_file` directory.

Note (from IgBLAST documentation)

> If you also want CDR3/FWR4 information, you need to supply a file that has information such as CDR3 stop for germline J genes (see optional_file/human_gl.aux for an example). This file can have any name and can be put anywhere as long as you supply it to the -auxiliary_data parameter when running IgBLAST(for example -auxiliary_data my_foler/my_file).

## Error: `[internal_data] cannot be found`. 

### Assign path to environment variable `IGDATA`

**Method:** 

```
export IGDATA=/Users/emoseley/ncbi-igblast-1.17.1/bin
```

This will help to solve the issue of `[internal_data] cannot be found`. 

Note that the `IGDATA` variable should:

1. point to the `bin` folder, not the `internal_data` folder.

2. use the full path (e.g. in mac `/Users/emoseley/ncbi-igblast-1.17.1/bin`) and NOT a relative path

3. The path should not contain any spaces (change your directory name if it does).
